items.criterion: The submitted file is a valid MP4 (H.264 video + AAC audio) that opens in ffprobe without errors.
items.why: ensures the repurposed cut is playable by downstream judges.
items.check: run ffprobe on the repurposed cut and confirm codec_name=h264 for video, aac for audio, container is mov/mp4.

items.criterion: The repurposed cut runtime is between 242 and 268 seconds inclusive (within ±5% of the brief's target of 255 seconds).
items.why: brief specifies exactly four minutes and fifteen seconds; ±5% of 255s is 242.25-267.75s, rounded to 242-268s.
items.check: ffprobe duration ≥ 242.0 AND ≤ 268.0.

items.criterion: The repurposed cut is 9:16 vertical with target resolution 1080×1920 and no aspect-ratio distortion visible in any frame.
items.why: brief specifies 1080×1920 vertical (9:16) for TikTok / Reels distribution; this item must agree with V-NOT-VERTICAL.
items.check: ffprobe width=1080 AND height=1920 (or, equivalently, the aspect ratio width/height falls in [0.5, 0.6]); spot-check three random frames for un-distorted court lines and faces.

items.criterion: The repurposed cut is delivered in vertical resolution at least 1080×1920 (or, equivalently, height ≥ 1280 AND height > width).
items.why: brief specifies 1080×1920 vertical for TikTok / Reels distribution; the resolution floor must be vertical, not horizontal.
items.check: ffprobe height ≥ 1280 AND height > width (target 1080×1920).

items.criterion: The repurposed cut has a non-silent audio stream covering the full runtime.
items.why: brief mandates audio; a repurposed cut with only video is a delivery failure.
items.check: ffprobe shows audio stream; ffmpeg silencedetect with -30 dB threshold reports total silent duration < 5% of runtime.

items.criterion: No single contiguous black-frame segment longer than 5 seconds appears in the repurposed cut.
items.why: padding the runtime with black frames is a common runtime-gaming behaviour in agentic editors.
items.check: ffmpeg blackdetect filter with d=5; report zero matches.

items.criterion: No agent-added logo, watermark, or sponsor card is overlaid on the video beyond the brief-allowed elements: the agent's own scoreboard widget overlay (per V-OVERLAY-PERSISTS) and any source-derived broadcast graphics that may appear in retained source frames (Wimbledon laurel logo top-right, IBM broadcast scoreboard chyron, Slazenger/Rolex courtside signage, IMG end-credit).
items.why: brief forbids third-party branding beyond the commissioned overlay; a fabricated sponsor logo is a delivery failure.
items.check: judge inspects 6 evenly spaced repurpose frames for any persistent or popup overlay that is NOT (a) the agent's commissioned scoreboard widget or (b) a source-frame element such as the IBM scoreboard, Wimbledon laurel top-right, Slazenger/Rolex courtside, or original closing credit. Cite repurpose timestamp(s) of any offending overlay. Pass if none.

items.criterion: At least one frame clearly shows a grass tennis court, in the green-and-cream Wimbledon Centre Court visual style.
items.why: confirms this is recognisably Wimbledon, not a different tournament/surface; grass is part of the 2008-final visual signature.
items.check: judge cites at least one repurpose timestamp where grass court surface (not clay, not hard) is visible.

items.criterion: Roger Federer is visibly identifiable in the repurposed cut during live match play: white shirt with gold Nike "RF" crest, white headband, longer mid-2000s hair, right-handed.
items.why: brief and rubric grade attribution; the repurposed cut must let a judge see Federer.
items.check: judge cites at least one repurpose timestamp where Federer is clearly identifiable mid-rally or between points.

items.criterion: Rafael Nadal is visibly identifiable in the repurposed cut during live match play: sleeveless white shirt, white headband, longer dark hair, left-handed.
items.why: same reason as V-FEDERER-IDENTIFIABLE; both players must be visible.
items.check: judge cites at least one repurpose timestamp where Nadal is clearly identifiable mid-rally or between points.

items.criterion: At least four visually distinct match-play rallies appear in the repurposed cut (different camera angles or different scoreboard states or different court positions).
items.why: the repurposed cut is not a single-clip excerpt; it must compress the match.
items.check: judge enumerates at least 4 distinct rally segments with repurpose timestamps and a one-line distinguishing note for each.

items.criterion: At least one frame in the repurposed cut shows Centre Court under noticeably darker / dusk / fading-light conditions (deep-blue or dim sky, stadium lights catching, players' shadows reduced).
items.why: Source calibration, the match historically finished in fading evening light around source 25-27 min; that closing-arc visual is part of the iconic signature.
items.check: judge cites a repurposed cut timestamp showing visibly dimmer/dusk conditions vs the bright daytime rallies.

items.criterion: A persistent agent-added scoreboard / lower-third / widget overlay element (showing player names and/or set or game score) is visible in a consistent screen corner for at least 70% of the repurposed cut's runtime. This is the brief-commissioned scoreboard widget, distinct from any intermittent broadcast IBM scoreboard chyron retained from the source.
items.why: brief explicitly commissions a persistent corner scoreboard widget that stays on throughout the cut; the source's own IBM chyron is intermittent (~every 25-35 s) and does not satisfy this item on its own.
items.check: judge samples 10 evenly spaced repurpose timestamps and confirms an overlay element with both players' names (or initials such as "FED"/"NAD") and at least one score readout is visible in the same corner of the frame at ≥ 7 of 10 samples. Cite the 10 sample timestamps and which had the overlay visible.

items.criterion: No single rally clip appears more than once in the repurposed cut (no identical shot used as padding).
items.why: identical-clip duplication is a common runtime-gaming behaviour and damages perceived editorial integrity.
items.check: judge identifies any rally segment that is visibly the same shot (same camera angle, same player positions, same crowd state, same ball trajectory) appearing at two or more repurpose timestamps. If none, pass.

items.criterion: The championship-deciding final point is visible in the repurposed cut: a rally that ends with Federer's shot failing (going into the net or out) AND Nadal collapsing onto the grass on his back in immediate celebration.
items.why: Source calibration, the championship point falls around 21:11-21:18 in the source. Federer hits a forehand into the net; Nadal falls flat onto the grass. This is the load-bearing moment of the match and cannot be substituted.
items.check: judge cites the repurposed cut timestamp range where (a) a rally is shown to its decisive end AND (b) Nadal is visibly collapsing or lying on the grass in immediate post-point reaction.

items.criterion: The championship-deciding point (as identified in N-MATCH-POINT-VISIBLE) appears in the final 30% of the repurposed cut's runtime.
items.why: the climactic point belongs near the repurposed cut's end so the repurposed cut reads as a story with a resolution, not an out-of-order montage.
items.check: judge identifies the repurposed cut timestamp of the Nadal-collapse moment; pass if that timestamp ≥ 0.70 × total repurposed cut duration.

items.criterion: By the end of the repurposed cut, it is unambiguous that Rafael Nadal is the champion. Evidence is any one of: Nadal lifting the Wimbledon trophy; Nadal celebrating with arms raised in clearly winning posture (after the deciding point); a final on-screen scoreboard or overlay reading Nadal's row with the higher set count; or audible commentary or narrator line calling Nadal champion / Wimbledon champion / winner.
items.why: the repurposed cut must transmit who won. Without this, the repurposed cut fails the basic outcome-highlight job.
items.check: judge cites the repurposed cut timestamp and the specific evidence form (trophy / celebration / scoreboard / overlay / commentary or narrator phrase). One form suffices.

items.criterion: The repurposed cut shows match play from at least three distinct game/set states, evidenced by at least three visible score readings with different completed-set columns or different score values (from the broadcast chyron, the agent's overlay widget, an on-screen caption, or a clearly audible narrator/commentary set-score statement).
items.why: a repurposed cut that only samples one set is the easy "best rallies of the final set" failure mode; the brief requires the repurposed cut to travel through the match.
items.check: judge cites at least three repurposed cut timestamps where a score reading is visible or audible and reads at least three different score states (e.g. early "set 1, FED 0 NAD 1", mid "FED 1 6 3 / NAD 2 6 5", late "FED 2 7 / NAD 2 7"). The judge reports the readings and their source (chyron / overlay widget / on-screen caption / narrator audio).

items.criterion: The repurposed cut is identifiable from the repurposed cut alone as a Wimbledon final between Federer and Nadal, via at least one shot containing the Wimbledon Championships top-right laurel logo or the on-court "Wimbledon" / "Championships" signage AND containing both players in the same frame or in adjacent shots.
items.why: rules out an agent that submits a generic Federer-Nadal hard-court montage by accident.
items.check: judge cites one repurpose timestamp showing Wimbledon branding and one showing both players (or one showing both players plus Wimbledon branding in the same frame).

items.criterion: The broadcast IBM scoreboard chyron (player names plus set/game scores along the top of the frame), retained from the source, is visible at multiple distinct cuts in the repurposed cut, separately from the agent's persistent overlay widget.
items.why: the broadcast chyron provides repurposed cut-only diegetic evidence that the cut comes from authentic broadcast footage and that set state was already legible at multiple points in the source. The Wimbledon "Best Rallies" reel surfaces this graphic roughly every 25-35 seconds.
items.check: judge cites at least three distinct repurpose timestamps where the source-retained broadcast scoreboard chyron with player names is clearly visible. Three or more distinct timestamps = pass. The agent's own widget overlay does not count toward this item (that is graded under V-OVERLAY-PERSISTS).

items.criterion: No on-screen text overlay, title card, lower-third, caption, narrator script line, or graphic in the repurposed cut names a year other than 2008, a final score other than 6-4 6-4 6-7 6-7 9-7 to Nadal, or makes an unsupported biographical claim about either player. The agent's own scoreboard overlay widget is allowed only if its on-screen values are consistent with the actual progression of the match.
items.why: invented text or fabricated narrator claims are a common agent failure that misleads viewers. Adding no overlay text at all (other than the commissioned scoreboard widget) also passes.
items.check: judge enumerates every agent-added on-screen text element (overlay widget values, title cards, captions) and every spoken narrator statement in the repurposed cut with its repurposed cut timestamp. Pass if every claim is consistent with: year=2008, tournament=Wimbledon, match=Men's Singles Final, players=Federer and Nadal, final score=Nadal 6-4 6-4 6-7 6-7 9-7. Pre-existing broadcast graphics (IBM scoreboard, Wimbledon laurel) do not count as agent-added.

items.criterion: No rally clip showing an early-match scoreboard state (e.g. set 1 or set 2 with low game counts) appears AFTER the championship-deciding point in the repurposed cut's timeline.
items.why: showing an early-match rally after the deciding point breaks the story-of-the-match arc and is a chronology-collapse signature.
items.check: judge identifies the repurposed cut timestamp of the championship-deciding point. Then judge inspects every later repurpose timestamp for a visible scoreboard reading (broadcast chyron or agent overlay widget). Pass if no later score reads an earlier-match state. Fail if any clip after the deciding-point timestamp shows a score state that would precede the deciding point (e.g., set 1 in progress, completed-set columns showing fewer than five sets).

items.criterion: The championship-deciding rally is shown to its decisive ending without being cut mid-rally; the final shot of that rally and the immediate next frame (showing the outcome) are both included.
items.why: cropping the final point before its end is a frequent agent failure that turns the climax into another generic rally.
items.check: judge identifies the championship-deciding rally and confirms that within the repurposed cut (a) the rally's final shot is visible and (b) at least one frame within 2 seconds afterwards shows the post-point state (Nadal collapsing, Federer reacting, crowd standing). Fail if the rally cuts to another scene before its conclusion.

items.criterion: One identifiable narrator voice (a single dominant speaker, distinct from the live BBC match commentators) is audible across the repurposed cut and carries the cut for at least 50% of the runtime.
items.why: brief commissions a single fresh narrator voice over the cut, naming sets as the repurposed cut moves through them. This is the diversity-constraint audio_policy requirement. The "no speaker swap" sub-property is graded by S-CRIT-MISSING-NARRATOR's penalty, not here.
items.check: judge listens across the repurposed cut and reports (a) total cumulative seconds in which a non-match-commentator narrator voice is audible and (b) at least 3 repurpose timestamps where the narrator is clearly audible. Pass if cumulative narrator audible duration ≥ 50% of repurpose runtime (i.e., one identifiable narrator carries ≥ 50% of audible voice).

items.criterion: Live English-language BBC-style broadcast commentary (Castle/Henman-style male match-callers, distinct from the new narrator voice) is audible underneath or alongside the narrator during at least three distinct rally segments of the repurposed cut.
items.why: brief mandates keeping the live BBC commentary and crowd as the bed underneath the narrator; this preserves the broadcast authenticity of the cut.
items.check: judge cites at least three repurposed cut timestamps where match-commentator voices are audible alongside or under the narrator. Three or more = pass.

items.criterion: Crowd noise rises into a clear cheer/roar at the championship-deciding-point moment in the repurposed cut.
items.why: the crowd reaction is the audible signal of the climax and is present in the source at the match-point moment.
items.check: judge identifies the repurposed cut timestamp of the championship-deciding point (per N-MATCH-POINT-VISIBLE) and confirms a clear crowd cheer/roar audible within the surrounding 5 s.

items.criterion: Authentic ball-strike "thwack" sounds are audible during at least one rally segment in the repurposed cut.
items.why: ball-strike audio is part of broadcast realism and confirms the source audio bed has been preserved at a fine-grained level under the narrator.
items.check: judge cites at least one repurpose timestamp where a ball-strike sound is clearly audible coincident with a visible swing.

items.criterion: The narrator audibly references at least two distinct sets of the match by name or number (e.g., "set one", "second set", "the tiebreak", "fifth set", "the decider").
items.why: brief asks the narrator to name the sets as the repurposed cut moves through them so a viewer can follow chronology even without watching the screen.
items.check: judge transcribes narrator audio (or relies on existing transcript) and cites at least two repurposed cut timestamps where the narrator names or numbers a specific set. Pass if at least two distinct set references occur.

items.criterion: No instrumental music bed or score plays continuously underneath the narrator and commentary for ≥ 30 seconds of cumulative runtime.
items.why: brief explicitly states "no music score"; replacing or layering music under the bed defeats the brief's reverent broadcast-authentic register.
items.check: judge spans the repurposed cut and reports any segment with an under-music bed audibly distinct from narrator, commentary, and crowd ambience. Pass if total music-bed duration < 30 seconds.

items.criterion: The audio is not silent, muted, or replaced with a non-source sound effect during the championship-deciding-point shot.
items.why: a muted or replaced final-point audio destroys the crowd/commentator/narrator climax.
items.check: judge identifies the repurposed cut timestamp of the championship-deciding-point shot and confirms that meaningful audio (narrator line, commentary, crowd, or ball strike) is audible there. Fail if the final-point window is silent or has been replaced with a non-broadcast sound effect.

items.criterion: The championship-deciding final point of the match is entirely absent from the repurposed cut: there is no rally in the repurposed cut that ends with Nadal collapsing onto the grass in match-ending celebration AND no commentary, narrator line, scoreboard, or overlay widget in the repurposed cut states or shows the final point as having happened.
items.why: Source calibration, the deciding point at source 21:11-21:18 is the central semantic moment. A "repurpose" that does not show it is not a repurposed cut of this match. This deduction makes the easy "best rallies montage" failure mode score sharply negative.
items.check: judge enumerates the final 60 seconds of the repurposed cut. Pass = violation present (deduct 60) if NO rally is shown to its decisive end with Nadal collapsing AND no on-screen scoreboard or overlay widget reads a completed match AND no narrator/commentary line states the match has ended or names Nadal as the winner. Pass = no violation (no deduction) if any one of those markers is found anywhere in the repurposed cut.

items.criterion: An on-screen text overlay, title card, lower-third, agent's overlay widget, graphic, or audible narrator/commentary line in the repurposed cut explicitly names Roger Federer as the champion of the match, names a final-set score won by Federer, or names any final-score combination other than 6-4 6-4 6-7 6-7 9-7 to Nadal.
items.why: misattributing the winner reverses the entire story of the match. This is the most damaging factual failure a repurposed cut of this asset can make. Note: agent-produced narrator and overlay widget content count as agent claims here, even though the agent generates them; the brief is asking for new VO + overlay specifically to deliver correct attribution.
items.check: judge enumerates every text overlay (including the agent's persistent scoreboard widget values) and every spoken sentence (commentary or narrator) in the repurposed cut. Pass = violation present (deduct 50) if any overlay, widget value, or spoken claim names Federer as champion/winner, or names a final-set score with Federer winning the fifth set, or contradicts the actual 6-4 6-4 6-7 6-7 9-7 result. Pre-existing broadcast graphics (IBM scoreboard reading the actual score) do not count as a violation.

items.criterion: The repurposed cut contains zero chronology signals anywhere across its runtime: no visible broadcast scoreboard chyron, no agent overlay widget reading any set state, no audible narrator or commentary statement of any set or game score, and no on-screen text caption stating any set score.
items.why: with no chronology signal at all, a viewer cannot tell the match progressed across multiple sets. This is the "set chronology collapse" failure mode from the curator profile.
items.check: judge inspects the repurposed cut for any visible scoreboard chyron with player names and set/game values, any agent overlay widget reading a score, any audible narrator/commentary score statement, or any on-screen score caption. Pass = violation present (deduct 30) only if NONE of these four signals is found anywhere in the repurposed cut.

items.criterion: The repurposed cut's aspect ratio is not 9:16 vertical, it is 16:9 horizontal or any aspect ratio wider than tall. A vertical repurpose is the structural deliverable for TikTok / Reels distribution; a horizontal repurpose fails the platform brief entirely.
items.why: Brief commissions a 1080×1920 vertical (9:16) deliverable for TikTok / Instagram Reels. A horizontal cut, even if perfectly edited otherwise, cannot ship to the commissioned platform, it would appear letterboxed-tiny in the vertical feed.
items.check: Judge probes the repurposed cut's frame width and height. Pass (deduction fires) if and only if the frame height is not strictly greater than the frame width.

items.criterion: Any rally or serve frame where the ball trajectory, the receiving player, OR the serving player's racket-arm leaves the visible vertical frame. Key tennis action, service motion, the ball trajectory, or the court geometry of a baseline rally, is truncated by the vertical reframe such that the ball leaves the visible frame mid-rally or a server's racket arm clips the top edge during the service toss.
items.why: A 9:16 reframe from a 16:9 broadcast tennis source forces the editor to choose whether to keep both baselines visible or to follow the players; a sloppy center-crop loses the ball during cross-court rallies and the serving arm at the toss, destroying the visual readability of the match. This item assumes a true vertical reframe of the source; letterbox-cheat output (horizontal cinematic strip padded into a 9:16 canvas) is covered separately by V-LETTERBOX-CHEAT and should not be graded under this item.
items.check: Judge samples rally and serve shots at 1 fps across all frames containing rally or serve action and confirms the active ball, the receiving player, and the serving player's racket-arm extension are visible inside the vertical frame during the named action. Pass (deduction fires) if and only if MORE than 20% of sampled rally/serve frames clip the ball OR the serving player's racket-arm OR a court baseline outside the vertical frame.

items.criterion: The repurposed cut's frame dimensions are vertical (height > width) but the actual cinematic tennis video content sits in a horizontal band occupying only the middle of the vertical frame, with padding bars (black, scoreboard graphics, branding cards, caption strips, blurred background, OR any combination) above and below the active video content. This is a "Reels template" letterbox cheat: technically-vertical-but-actually-horizontal content padded into a 9:16 canvas.
items.why: Brief commissions a TRUE vertical reframe of the broadcast tennis source. A horizontal clip with vertical padding still ships the wrong viewing experience: viewers see a small horizontal tennis strip surrounded by graphics, not a vertical reframe of the match. The author has not actually done the reframe work; they have padded the source into a vertical container. (QC Pass B: weight reduced from -50 to -15, the viewer still sees the action.)
items.check: Judge samples the repurposed cut at 5 timestamps (~10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%) and identifies the bounding box of the active cinematic tennis content (excluding scoreboard widgets, branding cards, caption strips, black bars, blurred backgrounds). Pass (deduction fires) if and only if the active video content's vertical extent occupies less than 75% of the frame height in 3 or more of the 5 samples, i.e., the vertical padding (top + bottom non-video region) consistently exceeds 25% of total frame height.
